name: tethertrace
description: Lets an agent test Android apps on your own phone over Wi-Fi: screen, input, installs, YAML flows and builds. Looking at the phone keeps your existing policy; touching it, installing, building and pairing are reviewed; raw shell is blocked. The server enforces its own policy too: read-only mode, per-app scope checked on the phone, confirmation and a local audit log. Off until you turn it on.
saferAlternatives: Start the server with tethertrace mcp --read-only: only the tools that look at the phone are listed, and nothing can tap, type, install, build or run a shell.
Start it with --package com.example.app: the server checks which app is in front before every read and every touch, and refuses when it is another app or it cannot tell.
Leave --allow-shell and --allow-build off (the default); the shell and build_project tools are then not listed at all.
Use --confirm interact,install so the server itself asks a person before each such call, and read ~/.tethertrace/audit.jsonl to see what was done.
These defaults match a server started as the tethertrace command. Started another way (for example node dist/cli.js mcp), it keeps Guard's normal handling.
